title: Ang 1426–1429: the ninth Guru's saloks
hookLine: fifty-seven saloks of the passing world and the Name that remains
tomorrow: the Granth closes on a plate holding three things. what are they?

cards: Notifications, plans, a stressful week: give it a month and most of it will be gone from memory. Guru Tegh Bahadur, the ninth Guru, keeps saying so in his saloks, starting on ang 1426.
In paraphrase: know this world as a dream, a passing show. And near the end of the set comes the answer to yesterday's question. In paraphrase: the Name remains, the holy remain, the Guru remains.

teach.b: The saloks are short couplets, plain and steady, and they keep returning to one thing: everything you can see is passing.

teach.h: FRIGHTEN NO ONE, FEAR NO ONE.
teach.b: Not to frighten anyone. A worry fades, a plan changes, even a house changes hands, and the saloks name that honestly, without drama.
One salok, in paraphrase, says it outright: the wise one frightens no one, and fears no one. And the close of the set holds up what doesn't pass. The Name remains.
The holy remain. The Guru remains.
It gathers the week. Farid's collar, and his heart like a jewel. Guru Arjan's praise, and the Bhatts' one light.
Waheguru, said in wonder before the results. Guru Nanak's love, with the head on the palm. Each one points at something that doesn't wash away with the month.
The ninth Guru's saloks say it plainly, and the walk through the Granth is almost home.

how: Guru Tegh Bahadur's saloks are read near the close of a full reading of the Granth, just before the Mundavani, and are sung at the bhog that completes it.

games.q: the ninth Guru's saloks — tap the pairs.
p: frightens no one, fears no one

s: the ninth Guru's saloks say nothing matters because it all passes
they say the world passes and the Name remains: something does stay.
one of the saloks says: frighten no one, and fear no one
that's the mark of the wise one, in the ninth Guru's saloks.

games.q: your friend's grandpa is moving out of the house he's lived in for decades. she says, 'so it all just disappears.' what do the ninth Guru's saloks give her?
o: houses pass like a dream; the saloks say the Name remains, and so do the holy.
it all disappears, so it's wiser never to get attached to anything at all.
the house stays forever, as long as the family keeps remembering it.
games.why: the saloks don't say nothing matters. they say what passes, passes, and name what remains: the Name, the holy, the Guru.

practice: Close your eyes and let the week's noise go by like traffic: the plans, the worries, the screens. Under it, keep one small thing steady, the breath, or the Name if you say it. Let everything else pass.

wordCard.voice: Ang 1426. Where the ninth Guru's saloks begin: the world passes like a dream, and the Name remains.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: naam, the Name, from the ninth Guru's salok near the close of the set: the Name remains.

carryVoice: Keep this close: the name remains, when everything else on the list has passed. Back tomorrow, at the seal.
